questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would not change even if Moses or Samuel pled for the people?
questions.a: He would still not act mercifully toward them.

questions.q: What will happen to the people of Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: Some will die, some will be killed, some will starve, and some will be taken far from home.

questions.q: What four things will happen to the people?
questions.a: Some will die in war, dogs will drag some away, birds will eat some, and beasts will eat some.

questions.q: What did King Manasseh do that caused Yahweh to make Judah a terror to all the kingdoms of the earth?
questions.a: He did wicked things in Jerusalem.

questions.q: Who will care about Jerusalem?
questions.a: No one will care about Jerusalem.

questions.q: What is Yahweh tired of doing for Jerusalem?
questions.a: He is tired of having mercy on Jerusalem.

questions.q: What has Yahweh’s people refused to do?
questions.a: They have refused to turn away from their evil behavior, so Yahweh will destroy them and take away their children.

questions.q: How many widows will there be in the land?
questions.a: There will be more widows than the grains of sand on the seashore.

questions.q: What will make the mother of seven children ashamed and embarrassed?
questions.a: Yahweh will have the enemy kill her children.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah say everyone in the land does to him?
questions.a: Everyone opposes him, quarrels with him, and curses him.

questions.q: When will Yahweh make Jeremiah’s enemies beg for help?
questions.a: He will make them beg for help in the time of calamity and distress.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, how strong are the enemies that will attack from the north?
questions.a: They are as strong as iron or bronze, and no one will be able to stop them.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh give the people’s wealth to their enemies?
questions.a: He will give it because of all the people’s sins.

questions.q: Where will the enemies take the people of Judah as prisoners?
questions.a: They will take them to a land they have never known before.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah ask Yahweh to do to the people who persecute him?
questions.a: He asks Yahweh to punish those who persecute him.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah do with Yahweh’s words?
questions.a: He gladly accepted Yahweh’s words, and they filled him with joy.

questions.q: What did Jeremiah do instead of joining people who were celebrating?
questions.a: He sat alone.

questions.q: What does Jeremiah compare Yahweh to when he feels Yahweh is not helping him?
questions.a: He compares Yahweh to a deceptive brook or water that is not reliable.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say Jeremiah must do to be restored?
questions.a: He must repent.

questions.q: What will Yahweh make Jeremiah like, to protect him from the people?
questions.a: Yahweh will make him like a wall of strong bronze.

questions.q: What kinds of people will Yahweh rescue Jeremiah from?
questions.a: He will rescue him from wicked people and cruel people.

commentary.text: The destruction of the wicked described. (Jer. 15:1-9) The prophet laments such messages, and is reproved. (Jer. 15:10-14) He supplicates pardon, and is promised protection. (Jer. 15:15-21)

Jer. 15:1-9 The Lord declares that even Moses and Samuel must have pleaded in vain. The putting of this as a case, though they should stand before him, shows that they do not, and that saints in heaven do not pray for saints on earth. The Jews were condemned to different kinds of misery by the righteous judgment of God, and the remnant would be driven away, like the chaff, into captivity. Then was the populous city made desolate. Bad examples and misused authority often produce fatal effects, even after men are dead, or have repented of their crimes: this should make all greatly dread being the occasion of sin in others.

Jer. 15:10-14 Jeremiah met with much contempt and reproach, when they ought to have blessed him, and God for him. It is a great and sufficient support to the people of God, that however troublesome their way may be, it shall be well with them in their latter end. God turns to the people. Shall the most hardy and vigorous of their efforts be able to contend with the counsel of God, or with the army of the Chaldeans? Let them hear their doom. The enemy will treat the prophet well. But the people who had great estates would be used hardly. All parts of the country had added to the national guilt; and let each take shame to itself.

Jer. 15:15-21 It is matter of comfort that we have a God, to whose knowledge of all things we may appeal. Jeremiah pleads with God for mercy and relief against his enemies, persecutors, and slanderers. It will be a comfort to God's ministers, when men despise them, if they have the testimony of their own consciences. But he complains, that he found little pleasure in his work. Some good people lose much of the pleasantness of religion by the fretfulness and uneasiness of their natural temper, which they indulge. The Lord called the prophet to cease from his distrust, and to return to his work. If he attended thereto, he might be assured the Lord would deliver him from his enemies. Those who are with God, and faithful to him, he will deliver from trouble or carry through it. Many things appear frightful, which do not at all hurt a real believer in Christ.
